name: Tuna, Bean & Avocado Salad

ingredients.name: tinned tuna in spring water, drained
tinned cannellini or butter beans, drained

steps: Gently fold the tuna, beans, tomato and avocado together in a bowl.
Mix the dressing ingredients in a small bowl and pour over.
description: A 10-minute tuna, white bean and avocado salad with a lemony yoghurt dressing.
whoItsFor: Anyone wanting a fast, high-protein lunch with healthy fats.
tips: Stuff into pita, pile onto a jacket potato or serve in a wholemeal roll.
Keeps a day in the fridge - add the avocado just before eating if prepping ahead.

name: Chicken & Vegie Filo Pie

ingredients.name: bay leaf or bouquet garni sachet
mixed vegetables (carrot, cauliflower, leek, cabbage, asparagus, baby corn, peas)

steps: Heat the oven to 200°C.
Gently poach the chicken in the stock, sherry and bay leaf in a covered pan for 15-20 minutes.
Add the bite-sized vegetables, cover and cook 5 minutes more; discard the bay leaf.
Move the chicken and veg to a deep pie dish; thicken the pan juices with the cornflour mixed into the milk, add herbs and pepper, and pour over.
Layer the filo, spraying every second sheet, lay it scrunched over the top, spray and bake until crisp and golden.
description: A big, lean chicken and vegetable pie under a crisp filo lid instead of buttery pastry.
whoItsFor: Lifters and endurance athletes wanting a hearty, 40g-protein comfort dinner.
tips: Brush the filo with egg white instead of oil to cut the fat further.
Skip the pastry and serve it as a casserole with rice or mash.

name: Easy Beef Hotpot
steps: Heat the oven to 180°C.
Shake the beef with the flour and paprika in a bag, then tip into a heavy casserole dish.
Add everything else and stir.
Press baking paper onto the surface, put the lid on tightly and bake for 2 hours without lifting the lid.
Check tenderness and seasoning, giving it longer if needed.
description: A no-fuss, oven-braised beef and root vegetable hotpot - everything into one pot.
whoItsFor: Strength athletes wanting a 50g-protein, iron-rich winter dinner.
tips: Serve with mashed potato and steamed greens.
Even better the next day - make it on the weekend for weeknight dinners.

name: Fast Fish & Rice Medley

ingredients.name: fresh red chilli, seeded and chopped
white fish fillets, in small pieces

steps: Cook the rice as per the packet.
Soften the onion and garlic in the oil, then add the tomatoes, chilli and wine and simmer 5 minutes.
Stir in the rice, capsicum, peas, fish and scallops, cover and cook 5 minutes until the fish is done.
Fold through the spinach until wilted.
description: A one-pan Australian Government recipe of fish, rice, tomato and vegetables - ready in about half an hour.
whoItsFor: Endurance athletes and lifters wanting a lean, carb-and-protein dinner.
tips: Frozen fish works fine; prawns can replace the scallops.
Check the tinned tomatoes are gluten-free if you need strict gluten-free.

name: Pumpkin, Spinach & Ricotta Lasagne

ingredients.name: pumpkin or sweet potato, peeled and sliced
English spinach or young silverbeet, washed and sliced
instant lasagne sheets, softened in hot water

steps: Heat the oven to 180°C. Steam the pumpkin for 3 minutes and cool; wilt the spinach in boiling water and drain well.
Mix the spinach with the ricotta, spring onion and parsley.
In a 33 x 23cm dish, layer 3 lasagne sheets with a third each of the pumpkin, sauce and ricotta mix; repeat twice and finish with lasagne.
For the topping, mix the eggs and flour smooth, whisk in the milk and stir over heat until thick, season and pour over.
Sprinkle with cheese and bake 30 minutes until golden.
description: A vegetarian lasagne layered with pumpkin, spinach and ricotta under a light egg-milk topping.
whoItsFor: Vegetarians wanting a 32g-protein dinner that feeds a family.
tips: Add a tin of lentils to the layers for even more protein and fibre.
Cut into squares and freeze individually for quick lunches.

name: Vegie Lentil Soup
steps: Soften the onion and garlic in a splash of water in a large pot.
Add the carrot, potato, parsnip and celery and cook 5 minutes.
Stir in the lentils, stock and tomato paste, bring to the boil, cover and simmer 30-35 minutes, stirring occasionally.
Stir in the parsley once the lentils and veg are tender.
description: A big-volume, almost fat-free red lentil and root vegetable soup.
whoItsFor: People cutting who want a filling, low-calorie lunch with plant protein.
tips: Vegan if you use water or vegetable stock instead of chicken stock.
Add a wholegrain roll to make it a more complete meal.

name: Hearty Minestrone Soup

ingredients.name: Brussels sprouts, finely sliced (or 1 cup sliced cabbage)
tinned four-bean mix, rinsed and drained

steps: Soften the onion and garlic in a little water in a large pot.
Add the tomatoes, carrot, celery, parsnip, tomato paste, bay leaf, stock and water and bring to the boil.
Add the pasta and simmer 15 minutes until tender.
Add the sprouts and beans and cook 5 minutes more.
description: A chunky Italian vegetable, bean and pasta soup with almost no fat.
whoItsFor: Anyone wanting a filling, low-calorie lunch with 10g protein per bowl.
tips: Swap the beans for lentils or butter beans, and the sprouts for spinach or peas.
Use vegetable stock to make it vegetarian.

name: Vegie Curry with Rice

ingredients.name: small piece ginger, peeled and sliced
red or green curry paste, to taste
cauliflower or broccoli florets, or green beans

steps: Cook the rice. Salt the eggplant slices, leave 30 minutes, rinse, pat dry and cube.
Gently soften the garlic, ginger and onion in the oil in a large saucepan, then stir in the curry paste over low heat.
Add all the vegetables and tomatoes, cover, bring to the boil and simmer 20-40 minutes until tender.
Stir in the coconut milk for 5 minutes, then the herbs, and serve with the rice.
description: A big, mild coconut vegetable curry with pumpkin, potato and eggplant, served with rice.
whoItsFor: Endurance athletes wanting a carb-heavy, plant-based dinner before big training days.
tips: Add a tin of chickpeas to lift the protein to a more useful level.
Many curry pastes contain shrimp - check the label if you need it vegetarian.

name: Savoury Carrot & Parsnip Muffins
steps: Heat the oven to 190°C and spray a 12-hole muffin tray.
Sift the flours into a bowl (tip the husks back in), add the spice and fold in the carrot, parsnip, cheese and herbs.
Mix the eggs, oil and milk and stir lightly into the dry mix - don't over-mix.
Spoon into the tray and bake 25 minutes until golden and firm.
Cool on a rack.
description: Savoury wholemeal muffins packed with grated carrot, parsnip and herbs.
whoItsFor: Anyone wanting a lunchbox or pre-training snack that isn't sweet.
tips: They freeze well - microwave from frozen for a warm snack.
Serve with cottage cheese or labneh to add protein.

name: BBQ Banana Parcels with Orange Yoghurt
steps: Heat the barbecue and fold four squares of foil to double thickness.
Put a banana in the middle of each, add half the passionfruit and fold the edges to seal.
Barbecue 5 minutes, then open and top with sliced strawberry and the rest of the passionfruit.
Serve with the yoghurt mixed with orange rind.
description: Warm barbecued banana parcels with passionfruit, strawberries and orange-zest yoghurt.
whoItsFor: Endurance athletes after an easy, fruity carb snack or a light dessert.
tips: Use Greek yoghurt to add more protein.
No barbecue? Bake the parcels at 200°C for about 10 minutes.
